evidence.requirements: Nearly everything in the brief is met. The start page shows title, date/time, price per guest and seats left (start.jpg; TastingCard.tsx:27-41). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (TastingCard.tsx:50). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (1-8) and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:167-215). The server refuses more guests than seats left and puts the error on the guests field (store.ts:74-83, app.ts:120-123). Errors appear next to the field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows "Booking confirmed", tasting, guests, total and reference (confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (index.ts:28, StaffPage.tsx:194-211). Signed in, staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button, and cancelling frees seats (staff.jpg; store.ts:102-127). Fully booked state: TastingCard.tsx:20-24 and BookingPage.tsx:101-110. Stack is React, Express, React Router, react-hook-form and Tailwind. Memory store, PORT defaults to 3000, interface in English. One deviation: for n=1 it shows "1 seat left" instead of the brief's literal "<n> seats left" (format.ts:53-55). This is a deliberate, documented choice (SPEC.md A4) but differs from the brief as written.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and insert run synchronously with no await between them (store.ts:71-96), and tests cover concurrent attempts (store.test.ts:73-82, 154-163). Booking exactly the remaining seats is allowed (store.test.ts:35-40). Seats left never goes below 0 (store.ts:68). Cancelled bookings no longer count toward seats and drop out of the staff list (store.ts:113-124), and cancelling twice is harmless. Tastings that have started cannot be booked, with Europe/Berlin time handled correctly (format.ts:40-47, store.test.ts:67-71). Malformed JSON gets a 400 and oversized bodies a 413 (app.ts:208-216). The client refreshes seats after a 409 (BookingPage.tsx:147). Minor: z.coerce.number would accept guests=true as 1 (schemas.ts:14). The booking rate limit of 20 per 15 minutes per IP (app.ts:24, 67-73) also counts successful bookings, so guests on shared winery Wi-Fi or behind NAT could be blocked.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and then uses timingSafeEqual (staff-auth.ts:10-14). Session tokens are 32 random bytes kept in memory with an 8-hour expiry, sent in an httpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie, and logout ends them on the server (staff-auth.ts:28-58, app.ts:153-166). Failed sign-ins are rate limited, and only failures count (app.ts:58-66). Helmet with CSP is enabled and the JSON body limit is 10kb (app.ts:45-54). Staff routes are protected by requireStaff (app.ts:74-80). The public booking lookup leaves out name and email (app.ts:27-40). React escapes all output. There are no secrets in code, and the app refuses sign-in when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.ts:144-147). Cookies are not marked Secure, which the README documents (README.md:71-74).
evidence.code_quality: Code is cleanly split into shared/server/client folders. createApp is a factory with injected store and clock, which makes it testable. Load states use discriminated unions (BookingPage.tsx:13-17). Errors are typed: BookingError (store.ts:20-29) and ApiError (api.ts:35-44). The Field and fieldProps helpers are reused across forms. Naming is clear, functions are small and the comments are relevant. There is no needless abstraction; the only redundancy is the one-line re-export in client/format.ts.
evidence.tests: Tests are thorough and tied to the brief. Store tests cover seat limits, the exact boundary, concurrency, cancellation, reference uniqueness and the start-time cutoff (store.test.ts). Guest API tests cover validation per field, 409 on seat shortage, 404, 422, malformed bodies, 413 and the rate limit (api-guest.test.ts). Staff API tests cover wrong password, unset password, cookie flags, lockout, forged cookie, cancel freeing seats, logout and proxy handling (api-staff.test.ts). Component tests use RTL and check accessible descriptions (book.test.tsx:69-71, staff.test.tsx). Playwright e2e covers the full guest-to-staff flow, a 375px layout and touch-target sizes (e2e/booking.spec.ts).
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: wine-red header with a gold rule, cream cards and serif headings (start.jpg). Cards are clear, with prominent "Book …" buttons. The form shows the running total and the error sits right under the email field (form.jpg). The confirmation is clean, with a large reference (confirmation.jpg). The staff view is tidy, with seats-left and booked counts per tasting (staff.jpg). There are fully booked and passed states, and e2e checks the phone layout. Weak points: the page is plain, with no imagery and an empty-feeling start page. In staff.jpg the reference column is slightly misaligned between groups. Cancel uses window.confirm.
evidence.accessibility: Every input has a label linked by htmlFor/id, and invalid fields get aria-invalid plus aria-describedby pointing to the error (Field.tsx:8-33). react-hook-form moves focus to the first invalid field (form.jpg shows the focused email field). Pages use landmark header/main/footer, articles and sections labelled by their headings, and dl lists for details. Focus-visible rings are present, touch targets are min-h-11, and the html lang is set. Weaknesses: inline field errors are not live regions, so a server-side 409 guests error is not announced. The gold #b8913f eyebrow text ("THANK YOU", "STAFF") on cream is about 2.6:1 contrast, which fails WCAG AA (ConfirmationPage.tsx:70, StaffPage.tsx:79).
evidence.simplicity: Dependencies are mainstream and fit the brief's request for established libraries: Express, React Router, react-hook-form with zod, and Tailwind. helmet and express-rate-limit add moderate weight. The code is a reasonable size for the scope. The time-zone helper (format.ts:23-47) and the passed-tasting logic go a bit beyond what the brief asks for, as do the trust-proxy option and booking rate limiting.
evidence.maintainability: README has run/build/test commands, an env var table, architecture notes and a candid Limitations section. SPEC.md records assumptions A1-A10 and success criteria; tasks/plan.md records architecture decisions. package-lock.json is present, with typecheck, lint, unit and e2e scripts. Gaps: no CI pipeline, no CHANGELOG or release/versioning approach beyond version 1.0.0, engines is ">=22" with no .nvmrc, no formal ADRs, and no separate staff manual (the README covers staff use only briefly).

unmet_requirements: Partly met: when one seat is left the label reads "1 seat left" instead of the brief's literal "<n> seats left" format (src/shared/format.ts:53-55; deliberate per SPEC.md A4)
strengths: Robust booking logic: synchronous seat check and insert, cancelled bookings free their seats, start-time cutoff, and shared zod validation enforced on the server with field-level errors
Solid staff security: constant-time password comparison, random server-side sessions in httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookies, sign-in rate limiting, helmet CSP, and no PII in the public booking lookup
Meaningful tests at every layer (store, API via supertest, components via RTL, Playwright e2e including phone layout and touch targets), plus a clear README and SPEC
issues: No CI pipeline or release/versioning process; Node version is only loosely constrained (engines >=22, no .nvmrc)
Booking rate limit of 20 attempts per 15 minutes per IP, successes included, could block legitimate guests on shared networks or NAT, e.g. the winery's own Wi-Fi
Accessibility gaps: gold eyebrow text fails AA contrast, and inline field errors (especially server 409 errors) are not announced to screen readers
review.verdict: This is a well-built, secure and well-tested booking app that meets the brief almost word for word and looks fitting for a small winery. I would ship it after adding CI, relaxing the per-IP booking limit and fixing the gold-text contrast.
